messages.content: "In a game of basketball, a player has a 60% chance of making a successful shot. In a particular match, the player attempts 10 shots. What is the probability that the player makes exactly 6 successful shots? Now, consider a different scenario where the player's success rate drops to 50% but the number of attempts remains the same. What is the probability of making exactly 6 successful shots in this scenario? Finally, consider a third scenario where the player's success rate remains at 50% but the number of attempts increases to 15. What is the probability of making exactly 6 successful shots in this third scenario?"

function.name: calc_binomial_prob
function.description: Calculates the probability of an outcome based on the binomial distribution Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

num_success.description: Number of times the event of interest has occurred.

prob_success.description: Probability of the event of interest on any single experiment. This is a float type value.

message.content:
**Background – Binomial Distribution**

For \(n\) independent trials where each trial succeeds with probability \(p\),
the probability of getting exactly \(k\) successes is  

\[
P(X=k)= \binom{n}{k}\,p^{\,k}(1-p)^{\,n-k}
      = \frac{n!}{k!(n-k)!}\;p^{\,k}(1-p)^{\,n-k}.
\]

Below we apply this formula to each of your three situations.



--------------------------------------------------------------------

### 1️⃣ Player’s shooting percentage = 60 %, attempts \(n=10\)

| Symbol | Value |
|--------|-------|
| \(n\) | 10 |
| \(k\) | 6 |
| \(p\) | 0.60 |

\[
\begin{aligned}
P_1 &= \binom{10}{6}\,(0.60)^6\,(0.40)^4   \\[4pt]
    &= 210 \times 0.046656 \times 0.0256     \\[4pt]
    &\approx 0.2512 .
\end{aligned}
\]

> **Result:** About **25.12 %** chance of exactly six made baskets.


--------------------------------------------------------------------

### 2️⃣ Shooting percentage falls to 50 %, still \(n=10\)

| Symbol | Value |
|--------|-------|
| \(n\) | 10 |
| \(k\) | 6 |
| \(p\) | 0.50 |

\[
\begin{aligned}
P_2 &= \binom{10}{6}\,(0.50)^6\,(0.50)^4   \\[4pt]
    &= 210 \times 0.015625 \times 0.0625   \\[4pt]
    &= 210 \times 0.0009765625            \\[4pt]
    &\approx 0.2051 .
\end{aligned}
\]

> **Result:** Roughly **20.51 %** probability of hitting exactly six shots when his accuracy is half‑half.



--------------------------------------------------------------------

### 3️⃣ Accuracy stays at 50 % but attempts increase to \(n=15\)

| Symbol | Value |
|--------|-------|
| \(n\) | 15 |
| \(k\) | 6 |
| \(p\) | 0.50 |

Here \(\displaystyle \binom{15}{6}=5005.\)

Because \(p=\tfrac12,\;(1-p)=\tfrac12\),

\[
\begin{aligned}
P_3 &= \binom{15}{6}\left(\tfrac12\right)^{6}\!\!
        \left(\tfrac12\right)^{9}\\[4pt]
    &= 5005\times\left(\tfrac12\right)^{15}\\[4pt]
    &= \frac{5005}{32\,768}\\[4pt]
    &\approx 0.1524 .
\end{aligned}
\]

> **Result:** Approximately **15.24 %** chance of scoring exactly six baskets from fifteen attempts at a 50 % hit rate.



--------------------------------------------------------------------
#### Quick recap

| Scenario | Attempts (\(n\)) | Success % (\(p\)) | Exact 6‑shot prob. |
|----------|------------------|-------------------|--------------------|
| A | 10 | 60 % | **~0.251** |
| B | 10 | 50 % | **~0.205** |
| C | 15 | 50 % | **~0.152** |

These figures come straight from the binomial probability mass function.
